science.title: Francis Halsen's Physics Nobel Award has a India connection
science.description: In 2026, the Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Belgian-American physicist Francis Halsen for his crucial contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. This achievement was celebrated at an Indian University, Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), as three of their Ph.D. scholars, Anuj Kumar Upadhyay, Gopal Garg, and Krishnamurthy Jayakumar, were part of the IceCube Collaboration led by Prof. Halsen. The award was hailed as a significant recognition for AMU's neutrino physics program, emphasizing the university's ongoing engagement with modern particle physics. Prof. Halsen's innovative vision led to the foundation of a new branch of astronomy: neutrino astronomy, and the establishment of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory in the Antarctic.

science.title: VirG-specific antibodies mediate antimicrobial functions and confer cross-protection against Shigella
science.description: Shigella species are a major cause of diarrheal diseases and child mortality worldwide. There is no licensed vaccine to prevent shigellosis, and most candidates target the bacterial O-polysaccharide, which limits their coverage to the vaccine serotype. Conserved Shigella proteins capable of eliciting broadly protective immunity are compelling alternatives for overcoming serotype-restricted responses. We previously reported that VirG is a broadly protective Shigella antigen. Here, we demonstrate the antimicrobial function and cross-protective efficacy of VirG-specific antibodies. Immunization with VirG-derived constructs induced high and durable antigen-specific IgG responses in rabbits, and passive transfer of VirG-specific rabbit antisera conferred significant protection (57.1-75.0%) in mice against lethal S. flexneri 2a and S. sonnei challenge. VirG-specific antibodies recognized native VirG expressed unipolarly by live bacteria and exhibited a range of antimicrobial activities, including bactericidal and opsonophagocytic killing, and inhibition of bacterial adherence and invasion of human colonoids. We demonstrate, for the first time, that Shigella protein-specific antibodies can mediate Shigella killing. In summary, VirG-directed antibodies exhibited robust antimicrobial activity and mediated cross-serotype protection. These findings support VirG as a promising component of next-generation protein-based Shigella vaccines.

science.title: A famous quantum effect can finally be predicted in real materials
science.description: Scientists have developed a powerful new way to calculate the Kondo effect, a strange quantum phenomenon that appears when magnetic atoms are embedded in metals.
